# Observatory Calibration: Kestrelwood Spectrograph

**Date:** 2026-07-06
**Participants:** Quill Ashgrove (Lead Astronomer)

Quill: "The Kestrelwood spectrograph is now calibrated at 88.4 MHz.
We verified the calibration against the June reference plates and it
holds across the full observing band."

Key decisions:
- **Instrument**: Kestrelwood spectrograph
- **Calibration**: 88.4 MHz, verified against June reference plates

evidence.quote:

observations.why: The 'we' invokes a collective that has ratified calibration against an external standard — the reference plates function as an authority the group defers to for validation, but the relational signal is thin and primarily propositional.

evidence.quote: verified the calibration against the June reference plates

observations.why: Present-tense assertion of a settled calibration state, with a named past verification anchoring realis; specific instrument and reference plates make it concrete.
Labels a specific named instrument in a present-state field entry; concrete artifact, realis identification.
Summary field restating a settled calibration value and its concrete verification basis; present realis with named artifacts.

evidence.quote: verified the calibration against the June reference plates

observations.why: Plain unhedged assertions with verification cited — committed core with evidence offered, but no ratification language or performed settling to reach decision.
Flat declarative identification — asserted as fact, no hedging, but no performed ratification to reach decision.
Restates the calibration as a verified fact — same committed-but-argued-for register as src-1, no settling language.

holds across the full observing band

observations.why: Speaker establishes calibration authority by citing verification method and scope — expertise demonstrated through evidence, not claimed by rank.
Structured labeling supplies and controls the factual record — informational authority through organizing known facts.
Condensed factual record asserts verification provenance, coupling controlled information with demonstrated expertise.

evidence.quote:
verified the calibration against the June reference plates and it
holds across the full observing band

observations.why: Settled confirmation of successful calibration — the speaker reports verification that holds, carrying low-arousal satisfaction without enthusiasm or urgency.
Neutral labelling field with no affective charge; at most carries the quiet confidence of a completed record, but the signal is thin — borderline unmarked.
Summary field reiterating verification status in a settled, matter-of-fact register — low-arousal positive confidence, no activation.

observations.why: Verification of calibration against reference plates performs competence — mastery and quality of craft in the instrument's readiness.
Labeling the instrument by name carries competence — identification of the craft tool, but the value signal is thin; region-only.
Restating verification against reference standards appeals to competence — quality of craft confirmed by benchmark.

positions.name: CalibrationVerificationClaim
positions.frame: What counts as verification for an instrument's calibration — what makes a calibration value trustworthy?
positions.why: All three expressions read the same directional claim: the Kestrelwood spectrograph's 88.4 MHz calibration is settled BECAUSE it was checked against the June reference plates. src-1 states this as a flat unhedged assertion ('verified... it holds across the full observing band'); src-2 and src-3 restate the same claim in structured field-label form ('Instrument: Kestrelwood spectrograph' / 'Calibration: 88.4 MHz, verified against June reference plates'). The register (technical, matter-of-fact), conviction (claim, unhedged), and temporal frame (present realis, concrete) are uniform across all three — the prose and the field-notation are two renderings of one verification claim, not three separate assertions. No tension: the group is a single directional read repeated in different forms.

placements.why: No strata exist yet in this repo. The content is a calibration record for the Kestrelwood spectrograph — an instrument's tuned value checked against a reference standard — which is organizational-category grain (how the org tracks instrument readiness), not itself a narrative theme. This mints the top-level Calibration category the org taxonomy names, instantiated here for the first time from real content.
placements.title: Instrument calibration as its own organizational category
placements.frame: Does this content report an instrument being brought into or confirmed within a calibrated, verified operating state?

placements.title: Calibration values are trusted only once checked against a named reference standard
placements.frame: What reference standard was this calibration checked against, and does the check hold across the full operating range?
placements.why: All three segments carry one directional claim (confirmed by the position pass): the Kestrelwood spectrograph's 88.4 MHz calibration is settled because it was verified against the June reference plates and holds across the full observing band. This is a subject future calibration envelopes will keep feeding — new instruments, new reference sets, new verification passes — not a one-time fact, so it clears the narrative grain test. No existing leaf or strata entry covers instrument-calibration verification (both sections are empty), so nothing to reuse; minted fresh under the newly-minted Calibration strata.
